essence: Established yet unaccomplishable, non-lord yet lord, place-and-time full of own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava-Lord, I praise.

sections.SUMMARY: Established yet unaccomplishable, non-lord yet lord, place-and-time full of own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava-Lord, I praise.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **ittham** — thus
* **svasaṃvedana** — self-consciousness
* **ādisiddha** — primordially established
* **asādhya** — unaccomplishable
* **ātman** — self
* **anīśa** — non-lord/lord
* **svaśaktisaṃpūrṇa** — full of own power
* **vadeśakāla** — place-and-time
* **nitya** — eternal
* **vibhu** — pervasive
* **bhairavanātha** — Bhairava-Lord
* **īḍe** — I praise
sections.EXPLANATION: Thus (ittham): self-consciousness (svasaṃvedanam), primordially established (ādisiddham), unaccomplishable (asādhyam) — the self (ātmānam), non-lord (anīśam), lord (īśam). Three incompatible predicates held without blinking: established from the beginning, never to be accomplished; non-lord and lord at once. Then the object of its only first-person act: whose place and time are full of own power — eternal (nityam), pervasive (vibhum): Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), I praise (īḍe). Vadeśakālam is obscure (possibly vaśe deśakālam, place-and-time under control); glossed neutrally, marked here, not smoothed. Praise, not proof, is what the paradox gets.
sections.BOUNDARY: 'vadeśakālam' is obscure; glossed neutrally, marked here.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is knowledge (jñāna) in the mode of paradox; the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at incompatible predicates held.
